claim: The protocol uses YYYY-MM-DD identifiers for the last date of backwards-incompatible change. The current protocol version is 2026-07-28.

2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header. List endpoints no longer vary per-connection. Cross-call state uses server-minted handles as ordinary tool arguments (SEP-2567).

2026-07-28 removes initialize and notifications/initialized. Every request carries version and client capabilities in _meta (SEP-2575). Earlier revisions 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 MUST start with initialize, then initialized.
Servers MUST implement server/discover. Clients MAY call it first to learn supported versions, or invoke any RPC inline and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.

Tasks leave the core protocol for official extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (SEP-2663). The persistent-task workflow in SEP-2322 (tasks/result, tasks/input_response) is historical; MRTR stays in core.

Multi Round-Trip Requests replace server-initiated JSON-RPC requests (SEP-2322). Servers MUST send server-to-client requests such as roots/list, sampling/createMessage, or elicitation/create using MRTR. The previous pattern is no longer supported. This is a breaking change.
Result responses MUST include resultType ("complete" / "input_required"). Clients MUST treat an absent resultType from earlier-protocol servers as "complete".

HTTP GET standalone SSE and resources/subscribe/unsubscribe are replaced by subscriptions/listen. SSE Last-Event-ID resumability is removed; clients MUST re-issue a broken stream as a new request with a new ID.

ping, logging/setLevel, notifications/roots/list_changed, notifications/elicitation/complete, and URL-mode elicitationId are removed from core. Log level is per-request _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel; servers MUST NOT emit notifications/message unless that field was present.

Roots, Sampling, Logging, and OAuth Dynamic Client Registration are deprecated with earliest removal the first revision on or after 2027-07-28. HTTP+SSE (deprecated since 2025-03-26) is scheduled three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final. A Deprecated feature remains in the spec; new implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it and existing implementations SHOULD migrate.

There is no negotiation handshake. Every request carries its protocol version and the server accepts or rejects independently. If the server does not implement the requested version it MUST respond with UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing the versions it does support. The client SHOULD select a mutually supported version from that list and retry, or surface an error.

Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection to establish context. Every request supplies this metadata in its _meta field. State that needs to span multiple requests MUST be referenced by an explicit identifier the client passes on each request.

Required request _meta fields are io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities. clientInfo is optional. A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC -32602 (Invalid params) and HTTP 400. Clients SHOULD include clientInfo on every request unless configured not to. Servers SHOULD include serverInfo in every result's _meta.

A server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared. If processing requires a capability absent from clientCapabilities, the server MUST return MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) and HTTP 400. Allocated 2026 error codes also include -32020 HeaderMismatch and -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersion.

SEP-2575 post-Final edits override the SEP body: clientInfo became optional (clients SHOULD include it); serverInfo moved to optional result _meta and DiscoverResult.serverInfo was removed (PR #3002); subscriptions/listen SHOULD send a graceful completion result before closing (PR #2953). Do not implement clientInfo as required from the SEP body.

A server that supports only this revision and receives leftover older-client traffic SHOULD: respond 405 Method Not Allowed to HTTP GET or DELETE on the MCP endpoint; ignore an Mcp-Session-Id header and not mint or echo session IDs; ignore Last-Event-ID (streams are not resumable).

Every POST to the MCP endpoint MUST include MCP-Protocol-Version matching body _meta protocolVersion; mismatch MUST be 400 HeaderMismatch (-32020). Unsupported version MUST be 400 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. Unknown RPC method MUST be 404 -32601. Mcp-Method is REQUIRED on all requests; Mcp-Name is REQUIRED for tools/call, resources/read, and prompts/get. Servers that process the body MUST reject header/body mismatches with 400 and -32020.

Clients MUST include an Accept header listing both application/json and text/event-stream. The POST body MUST be a single JSON-RPC request or notification; the client MUST NOT send JSON-RPC responses. stdio has no header layer: all request metadata is carried inline in the JSON-RPC body.

x-mcp-header is optional for servers but clients MUST support it. When a tool definition includes x-mcp-header annotations, conforming clients MUST mirror the designated parameter values into HTTP headers. Streamable HTTP clients MUST exclude from tools/list any tool whose x-mcp-header values violate the constraints.

stdio messages are newline-delimited and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines. The server MUST NOT write anything to stdout that is not a valid MCP message and MUST NOT write JSON-RPC requests to stdout (server-to-client interactions use InputRequiredResult). The client MUST NOT write JSON-RPC responses. To cancel, the client MUST send notifications/cancelled; servers SHOULD stop work as soon as practical and MUST NOT send any further messages for that request. Servers SHOULD exit promptly when stdin is closed.

A dual-era stdio client SHOULD probe with server/discover before any other request. DiscoverResult or a recognized modern error such as UnsupportedProtocolVersionError means stay modern and do not fall back to initialize. Any other error or a timeout means legacy; fall back to initialize. Fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific error code. A modern-only client need not probe, but probing is RECOMMENDED so a legacy server does not silently execute an era-ambiguous method such as tools/call.

SEP-2575's historical Backward Compatibility section said a dual-era stdio client should fall back to initialize if server/discover returns Unsupported protocol version or Method not found. The current stdio page contradicts that: a recognized modern error including UnsupportedProtocolVersionError means do not fall back. Post-Final spec edits are not in the SEP body; current spec wins.

Servers MAY send InputRequiredResult only on prompts/get, resources/read, and tools/call, and MUST NOT on any other client request. Every InputRequiredResult MUST include at least one of inputRequests or requestState. Servers MUST NOT send inputRequests the client has not declared. The JSON-RPC id MUST differ between the initial request and the retry. HTTP servers MUST NOT send independent JSON-RPC requests on the SSE stream.

If a client request contains requestState, servers MUST treat it as attacker-controlled input. If it influences authorization, resource access, or business logic, servers MUST protect its integrity (HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification. Servers SHOULD bind principal, TTL, and originating-request identifier inside the integrity-protected payload. Single-use requestState MUST be enforced server-side. Clients MUST echo the exact value and MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or assume anything about its contents.

The server MUST NOT send notification types the client has not explicitly requested. It MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message carrying io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId and MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before that. On stdio, clients MUST use that field to correlate notifications, and after reconnect the client MUST re-send subscriptions/listen — the server holds no subscription state across reconnections. When ending a subscription on its own initiative the server SHOULD respond to the original subscriptions/listen with a completion result before closing the stream.

notifications/message is request-scoped: the server MUST NOT emit it for a request that lacks io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel, and MUST NOT deliver it on a subscriptions/listen stream. Protocol Logging is deprecated; new implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it and existing implementations SHOULD migrate to stderr (stdio) or OpenTelemetry. Log messages MUST NOT contain credentials, PII, or internal system details that could aid attacks.

Servers that declare tools MUST respond to tools/list; the set MUST NOT vary per-connection or as a side effect of other requests on the connection, though it MAY vary by authorization. Servers SHOULD return tools in deterministic order. If outputSchema is provided, servers MUST provide conforming structured results and clients SHOULD validate them. Clients and servers MUST support JSON Schema 2020-12 for schemas without $schema and MUST NOT automatically dereference $ref values that resolve to a network URI (opt-in fetch MUST be disabled by default and SHOULD enforce a host allowlist). Clients MUST consider tool annotations untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

Authorization is OPTIONAL. HTTP implementations SHOULD conform to the authorization spec; STDIO implementations SHOULD NOT, and should retrieve credentials from the environment instead. When used: MCP servers MUST implement RFC 9728; clients MUST use it for authorization-server discovery; authorization servers MUST provide at least one of RFC 8414 or OIDC Discovery 1.0 and clients MUST support both; clients MUST implement RFC 8707 resource indicators; Authorization: Bearer MUST be on every HTTP request and MUST NOT be in the query string; servers MUST validate audience-bound tokens and MUST 401 invalid or expired tokens; servers MUST NOT accept or transit tokens not issued for them. CIMD SHOULD; DCR MAY but is deprecated.

Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding. If Origin is present and invalid, servers MUST respond HTTP 403 (body MAY be a JSON-RPC error with no id). When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost rather than 0.0.0.0. Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections. Allowlist, bind address, and what counts as invalid Origin are application configuration.

Servers MUST validate all tool inputs, implement proper access controls, rate-limit tool invocations, and sanitize tool outputs. The spec does not define a rate-limit algorithm, headers, or error code for too many tool calls — that is application policy. Implementations SHOULD cap schema composition depth, subschema count, and validation time. Intermediaries SHOULD verify MCP-Protocol-Version before trusting mirrored headers for routing or rate-limiting.

A handle is a name, not a capability. MCP servers that implement authorization MUST verify all inbound requests and MUST NOT treat possession of a state handle as authentication. MCP servers MUST NOT accept any tokens that were not explicitly issued for the MCP server (token passthrough forbidden).
SEP-2549: servers MUST provide ttlMs on list/read results and ttlMs MUST be >= 0. cacheScope (public vs private) and freshness are chosen by the server application.

The specification permits a modern-only server and does not require dual-era. A server that wishes to support both legacy clients (initialize handshake) and modern clients (per-request metadata) MAY implement both behaviors, including concurrently on the same endpoint or process. G4 (McpProtocol.v2026_07_28 only, no mixed protocol lists) is a product choice the spec permits, not a spec requirement. The versioning-page example supported: ["2026-07-28", "2025-11-25"] illustrates a dual-era server; it is not a requirement that every server list both.

Legacy client × modern (G4) server fails with no fall-forward. stdio: the server rejects initialize with an implementation-defined JSON-RPC error (unknown method and missing required _meta). HTTP: the request is missing required headers and is rejected per server validation with 400; a deprecated HTTP+SSE client fails at its opening GET. A modern-only server SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to initialize; a bare -32601 with no supported list is spec-legal but against that SHOULD.

A G4 server that implements server/discover (MUST) is unambiguously modern to dual-era probing clients: DiscoverResult or a recognized modern error means they will not fall back to initialize. A G4 server missing server/discover would look legacy (any other error or timeout → initialize fallback) and would itself violate the 2026-07-28 MUST. SEP-2575 rejected keeping initialize as an optional parallel path; a G4 modern-only server is the design the SEP preferred. Dual-era is an interoperability concession (MAY), not the intended steady state.

A G4 Streamable HTTP server SHOULD answer GET/DELETE with 405, ignore Mcp-Session-Id, and ignore Last-Event-ID. It MUST still implement server/discover, required headers, Origin checks, and UnsupportedProtocolVersionError with a supported list that under G4 contains only "2026-07-28". A client that then sends protocolVersion 2025-11-25 MUST get UnsupportedProtocolVersionError with data.supported: ["2026-07-28"].

G6 (external agent clients do not gate the flip) is consistent with the spec matrix only if those clients are already modern or dual-era. A still-legacy external client cannot talk to a G4 server; the spec says that outcome is expected. Dual-era in-repo clients SHOULD probe on stdio and MAY probe on HTTP and will not fall back if server/discover succeeds. If in-repo clients are also flipped to modern-only they SHOULD NOT implement initialize fallback; probing is only a deterministic-failure aid against other people's legacy servers.
